title: FairLex: A Multilingual Benchmark for Evaluating Fairness in Legal Text Processing

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring performance disparity (macro-F1 score equal risk) across gender groups (male vs. female) of applicants or defendants in legal text classification tasks.
Comparing classification performance (macro-F1) across different applicant age brackets (e.g., <=35, <=65, >65) in predicting violations for the European Court of Human Rights.
Evaluating model performance disparities based on the defendant state (e.g., Eastern European vs. the rest) or court region of origin across multiple legal jurisdictions.
Assessing performance gaps in legal judgment predictions for cases written in different languages (German, French, Italian) within the Swiss Federal Supreme Court dataset.
Measuring classification performance parity based on the ideological direction (liberal vs. conservative) of US Supreme Court decisions.
Comparing legal topic classification performance disparities across different types of legal respondents (e.g., person, public entity, organization, facility).
Evaluating macro-F1 performance differences across specific legal fields (e.g., public law, penal law, civil law) to measure disparity in how models handle different areas of law.
